quotes.quote: The metals markets are cyclical
Mining companies must continually replace reserves depleted by production to maintain production levels over the long term and provide a return on invested capital.

fade_years.why: I use 10 years for the margin and growth to fade from the year-5 level to the long-run level. Gold is a cyclical market, and a margin far above the company's history normalises only gradually. Reserve replacement and a long-lived asset base also slow the move, so a short fade would be too fast and a 20-year fade too slow.

long_run_op_margin.why: The filed history (2012 margin 0.3375) and gold's long-run history imply a through-cycle margin around 0.25-0.30. Gold now trades at multiples of its past levels against AISC of about $1,500, so I keep about half of the gap, giving 0.38. The range is wide because the gold price path is unknowable from these filings.

Newmont expects unit costs to trend higher in 2027

op_margin.why: 2026 should be about 52%, since nine-month income before tax was 10,792 on sales of 19,788 and Q4 costs step up. Margins then compress because management expects higher unit costs in 2027 (inflation, diesel, Australian dollar, gold-linked royalties, lower co-product credits) and the gold price is assumed to ease from current levels. Per the base rates, a margin well above the long-run median keeps only part of the gap.

After that, volumes are about flat (the production guide is 5.26 Moz) and Peñasquito silver falls. The gold price is assumed to drift down from its high level, so revenue is flat to slightly lower before returning to modest growth.

terminal_growth.why: This is a mature gold producer that must replace depleted reserves to hold output, so long-run growth is nominal GDP-like at best, set a little under the filed anchor of 0.0375 and well under the cost of equity.

Year 1 (2026) should show a large revenue jump from price, then flat or lower revenue as costs rise and prices partly normalise.
